newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat to weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat to weaker.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices remained mired in inactivity at midday, with prices flat to modestly weaker, traders said.

"Munis probably are an 01, an 02 (basis points) easier with not nearly as many bid wanteds as yesterday," one trader said. Though players were better sellers than buyers, no rush was on to unload bonds, he said.

"The market is very resilient," the trader said. "If they get anything close to their offering, it seems (players) are more apt to move their bonds, but I don't see any panic or distress sellng at all."
A second trader described the market as "basically unchanged."
"There is just nothing going on at all," he said. "I just think the absolute levels are high, (and) municipals are at the mercy of all the other markets."
With U.S. Treasuries "basically stalled out here," munis have little room to run, he said.
"We don't control our destiny, and that's basically the problem," he said.

While some of the deals that priced this week, including a $273 million California Public Works offering, benefitted from demand for new issues, players are selling seasoned issues to make room, the trader said.

"There's a lot of money out there for new issues, but it's the same old, same old," he said. "They buy the new issues and they sell stuff to pay for it either today or two weeks from now when the thing settles."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 11/32 at 100-8/32 to yield 6.61 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 13/32 at 117-11/32. The March T-bond contract was down 12/32 at 113-8/32. The MOB spread was 131 ticks.
Morning economic news included the U.S. Labor Department's report that initial state jobless benefit claims rose to 309,000 in the week ended Feb 15, from a revised 308,000 the previous week.

Also Thursday, the Commerce Department said construction starts on new homes and apartments rose two percent in January to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.35 million. That followed an 11 percent drop in December.
The figure was lower than expectations, which called for a 1.42 million annual rate.

In new issues, Lehman Brothers said it won $56 million Virginia Public School Authority notes at a true interest cost of 4.171 percent. Ahead in Thursday competitive action, a $65.5 million Arlington Independent School District, Texas, deal, set for 1400 EST.
On the negotiated side, an expected $65 million University of Pittsburgh deal via PNC Capital Markets tops the list.
As for Wednesday's offerings, a $59.4 million balance was reported on Florida Board of Education's $189.8 million deal.

Looking ahead, the Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia plans a $200 million refunding of its senior lien bonds this week or next week, depending on market conditions Ronald Vazquez, vice president of financial services said. JP Morgan Securities is senior manager for the negotiated deal, he said.
